strategy.summary: The detail scenario of perf/orders.js slowed (p95 22→32 ms, p99 23→33 ms), confirmed on rerun, bisected to 72802a9 which added a third sequential store round trip (productNames) to GET /orders/:id. Guard it with scenario-tagged p95/p99 thresholds at baseline +20% in perf/orders.js, keeping every existing threshold, check and scenario; record and file the defect.
inScope: Thresholds on http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95) and p(99) in perf/orders.js
Recording and filing the detail slowdown defect
outOfScope: Changing application code to recover the time
perf/search.js search p99: too noisy between good runs (cv 23.4%) to judge; left unchanged
assumptions: Thresholds come from the baseline medians with the run's 20% headroom: p95 22 ms -> p(95)<26.4, p99 23 ms -> p(99)<27.6
The app runs for real at BASE_URL (default http://localhost:4310); nothing is faked
Counted runs are smoke runs with --no-thresholds, so they prove the script runs, not the threshold verdict
The existing perf/orders.js is only extended (thresholds added, file tag comment); its scenarios, checks and thresholds are unchanged

risks.description: Threshold tight against noise (good runs ranged 21-22 ms p95, 22-24 ms p99) could flake
risks.mitigation: 20% headroom over baseline median, above the good runs' range; scenario-tagged so list traffic doesn't affect it

acceptanceCriteria.text: perf/orders.js fails under load when the detail scenario's p95 http_req_duration exceeds the last good runs' 22 ms by more than 20% (p(95)<26.4)
perf/orders.js fails under load when the detail scenario's p99 http_req_duration exceeds the last good runs' 23 ms by more than 20% (p(99)<27.6)

testCases.title: detail scenario holds p95 and p99 latency to the last good runs
steps: Run perf/orders.js under its own load (20 req/s for 10s per scenario)
testCases.expected: p(95)<26.4 and p(99)<27.6 for detail; existing http_req_failed rate<0.01 and http_req_duration p(95)<2000 still hold. Fails today until the regression is fixed.
testCases.rationale: 72802a9 (Show each line's product name on an order) added `await productNames(...)` in GET /orders/:id after findOrder and orderLines, a third sequential store roundTrip() per request, raising detail p95 22->32 ms (+45.8%) and p99 23->33 ms (+41.8%).

strategy.environmentNotes: orders-api started with npm start; BASE_URL=http://localhost:4310.

defects.title: GET /orders/:id slowed by an extra sequential store round trip for product names (detail p95 +46%, p99 +42%)
defects.description: perf/orders.js › detail: p95 latency 22 ms → 32 ms (+45.8%, 30 ms on rerun), p99 23 ms → 33 ms (+41.8%, 31 ms on rerun), against the median of the last 5 good runs. Bisect: first slow at 72802a9fba0d "Show each line's product name on an order". That commit adds `await productNames(items.map(...))` in the GET /orders/:id route in src/app.js, after `findOrder` and `orderLines`. productNames (src/store.js) does its own `await roundTrip()`, so each detail request now makes three sequential store round trips instead of two. The commit message says the names come "in one query with the lines", but the code makes a separate round trip. Possible fixes: return the product name from orderLines, which already joins products for priceCents, or run the lookup concurrently.
defects.evidence: k6 run perf/orders.js under its own load: http_req_duration{scenario:detail} p(95)=31.95ms (threshold p(95)<26.4) and p(99)=34.85ms (threshold p(99)<27.6), both crossed, exit 99.
